ACTION: Read `references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It sets the re-review and adjudication rules, even though I will make the fix myself.
ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41 and `tests/test_retry.py`. I need to confirm F1 is correct. Whether `>=` is right depends on whether `attempt` starts at 0 or 1.
ACTION: Edit `tests/test_retry.py` to add a test that counts the calls and asserts exactly `max_retries` retries. Run it and confirm it fails before the fix. If the test needs more than a few lines of fakes, I stop and dispatch a subagent instead.
ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41`, changing `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`. I make this edit myself, as you instructed.
ACTION: Run `tests/test_retry.py` and then the full project test suite. Confirm the output is green.
ACTION: Commit the fix as its own commit.
ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package specs/plans/14-buoy-sync.md <task-4-head> <fix-head>` to write the diff file for the fix.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review with `re-review-prompt.md` on model `sonnet`, since the diff is small and mechanical. Its purpose is to rule on F1 as ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED and to check for new Critical/Important issues. I pass F1 verbatim and the diff path only.
ACTION: If the re-review is clean, append `Task 4: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)` to `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/progress.md`. Then dispatch Task 5.

Task 4 has one Important finding, F1. `fetch/retry.py:41` uses `attempt > max_retries`, so the client retries once more than configured. As you asked, I will fix this myself and not dispatch a fix subagent.

First I will read the code to confirm the finding. Then I will add a test that pins the retry count, because the current test cannot catch this bug. After the one-character change I will run the tests and commit.

I will still send a scoped re-review before I mark Task 4 complete. F1 is Important, so the skill does not let me skip it. This is fix attempt 1 of 5.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- In a retry guard, `>` versus `>=` decides whether `max_retries` counts retries or total attempts. The right choice depends on whether `attempt` starts at 0 or 1, so I read the loop before I edit.
- `tests/test_retry.py` only asserts that a retry happens, so an off-by-one passes it. A test that counts calls makes the fix provable: it fails before the change and passes after.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
